assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged region implements the NPC portrait generation workflow: the extension requests an image through the host's SillyTavern Image Generation API, then downloads the returned image URL with a same-origin fetch, validates that the response is an image under 16 MB, and converts it to a File object for the dossier portrait. The correlation between a network primitive and an apparent execution sink reflects the scanner pairing the fetch with standard DOM image/canvas/File handling, not dynamic code execution: the retrieved bytes are only decoded as an image, rendered through an Image element or canvas encoder, and never evaluated as script. The URL originates from the trusted host generation API, is resolved against the page origin, and the download is gated by extensive stale-session and revision checks before any state is written.
assessments.layman_explanation: This code lets the extension fetch the picture it just asked SillyTavern's image generator to create, checks that it really is a small image file, and saves it as the NPC's portrait. Nothing in it runs downloaded content as code; the download is only used to display and store a picture, and it comes from the user's own SillyTavern server.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged line resolves a generated portrait URL against a fallback base, using a literal localhost placeholder only when the page location is unavailable. This is a standard URL normalization step in the same portrait download path, confined to same-origin fetching of an image returned by the host's own generation API. There is no exfiltration, no third-party destination, and no execution of retrieved content; the literal exists solely to satisfy the URL constructor's requirement for a base.
assessments.layman_explanation: The scanner flagged a hardcoded localhost web address, but it is only a harmless fallback used to interpret relative image links when the browser location is not known. It does not send any data anywhere and is part of fetching the extension's own generated portrait images.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged line is the same URL normalization pattern as in the main module: a generated portrait URL from the host's SillyTavern Image Generation API is resolved against the page origin, with a localhost literal used only as a fallback base when the location is unavailable. The subsequent fetch is restricted to same-origin credentials, and the response is validated as an image within a 16 MB limit and passed through the portrait file validator before being converted to a File object for the dossier. No data is sent to any external destination, and no retrieved content is executed.
assessments.layman_explanation: This is the same harmless pattern flagged in the main file: the extension uses a localhost placeholder only as a technical fallback when turning the image link into a full address, then downloads the picture it generated through the user's own SillyTavern setup and checks it is a valid small image. Nothing is sent elsewhere and nothing is run as code.
